ranking.note: Raised to P1: it is the direct prerequisite for the P1 #10102 and for #19460/#19461, so it cannot sit a band below the work it unblocks.
Raised to P1 for consistency with #35932: both fix use-after-free/termination races in IPC connection teardown, the same class of reliability defect.
Raised to P2 to match #36106: both are bitcoin-wrapper platform bugs that make multiprocess binaries behave incorrectly for real users/harnesses.

inconsistencies: Dependency chain, review in this order: #36520 (crash hardening) → #29409 (Chain over IPC) → #10102 (multiprocess binaries) → #19460 (wallet -ipcconnect) → #19461 (gui -ipcconnect). #19461 contains a single unique commit and is pointless to review before its parents.

#32387 (ipc: add windows support) states it 'fixes the Windows wrapper executable to properly await child processes', which is exactly what #36105 does standalone. These overlap; review #36105 first as the smaller, self-contained fix and have #32387 rebase on it rather than carrying a duplicate change.
#36190 only tests behaviour introduced by #36105; it is not reviewable independently and should follow it.
#35932 and #36097 both carry temporary libmultiprocess subtree commits (bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#335 and #342). Their subtree bumps need to be sequenced so the second does not revert the first.

#29409 and #36520 describe their dependency in opposite directions on the two cards (#29409 'depends on #36520'; #36520 'before PR 29409 exposes the Chain interface'). Both readings agree #36520 lands first; treat #36520 as the base.
result.notes: The category is dominated by one author's stacked series; most of the P2 band is sequential work on the same project rather than independent items, so reviewer time spent on the base PRs (#36520, #29409, #10102) has leverage over everything below it. Crash/UAF fixes in connection teardown (#35932, #36572) and node hardening against hostile IPC input (#36520) are the only items affecting people running multiprocess builds today, which is why they sit in P1 alongside the project-defining PR.
